summary: The root "rjz" primarily describes a camel's disease. It also refers to reciting a specific poetic meter called "rajaz.
lane: 1 رَجِزَ ذ , [aor. رَجَزَ ,] (S,) inf. n. رَجَزٌ , (TA,) He (a camel) had the disease termed رَجَزٌ [expl. below]. (S.) -A2- رَجَزَ , (S, Msb, K,) aor. رَجُزَ , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. رَجْزٌ , (TA,) He said, spoke, uttered, or recited, poetry, or verse, of the metre termed رَجَزٌ ; [see this word below;] he spoke in verse of that metre; he poetized, or versified, in that metre; as also ; (S, * Msb, K, * TA;) and in like manner , he composed verses of that metre. (Ibn-Buzurj, L in art. قصد .) You say also, رَجَزَبِهِ He recited to him ( أَنْشَدَهُ [so in more than one MS. copy of the K, and in the TA, but in the CK أَنْشَدَ , without the affixed pronoun, which is probably wrong,]) a poem of that metre; as also , (K, TA,) inf. n. تَرْجِيزٌ . (TA.) And He urged, or excited, his camels by singing رَجَز , or his رَجَز : so accord. to different copies of the K. (TA.) -b2- [Hence,] رَجَزَتِ الرِّيحُ , inf. n. رَجْزٌ , (assumed tropical:) The wind was continuous, or lasting. (TA.) And الرَّعْدُ (tropical:) The thunder made uninterrupted sounds, like the recitation of the رَاجِز : (A, TA:) or, as also , made a sound: (K:) or made consecutive sounds. (TA.) And البَحْرُ بَآذِيِّهِ (tropical:) [ The sea makes a continuous sound, or murmuring, with its waves ]; as also . (A, TA.) [And hence, perhaps,] السَّحَابُ (tropical:) The clouds moved slowly by reason of the abundance of their water. (K, TA.) [See also 6.]

headwords.def: [aor. رَجَزَ,] (S,) inf. n. رَجَزٌ, (TA,) He (a camel) had the disease termed رَجَزٌ [expl. below]. (S.) رَجَزَ, (S, Msb, K,) aor. رَجُزَ, (Msb, TA,) inf. n. رَجْزٌ, (TA,) He said, spoke, uttered, or recited, poetry, or verse, of the metre termed رَجَزٌ; [see this word below;] he spoke in verse of that metre; he poetized, or versified, in that metre; as also; (S, * Msb, K, * TA;) and in like manner, he composed verses of that metre. (Ibn-Buzurj, L in art.
راجز صَاحِبَهُ [ He recited verses, or poetry, of the metre termed رَجَز with his companion: or vied with him in doing so: see 6]. (A.)

i. q. تَنَازَعُوا الرَّجَزَ بَيْنَهُمْ, (A, K,) and تَعَاطَوْهُ, (TA,) i. e. They recited verses, or poetry, of the metre termed رَجَز, one with another: (TK:) [or vied, one with another, in doing so. ] [Hence,] تراجز السَّحَابُ (tropical:) [ The clouds combined, one with another, in uninterrupted thundering ]. (A.) [See also 1.]
: see the next paragraph, in four places.

properly signifies Commotion, agitation, or convulsion; and consecutiveness of motions. (TA.) Hence, (TA,) Punishment (Aboo-Is-hák, S, Mgh, Msb, K) [like رِجْسٌ ] that agitates by its vehemence, and occasions vehement consecutive commotions; (Aboo-Is-hák, Mgh, * TA;) as also: (K:) so in the Kur vii. 131; (Aboo-Is-hák;) and in ii. 56, and vii. 162, and xxix. 33. (S.) Conduct that leads to punishment: so, accord. to some, in the Kur lxxiv.

A certain disease which attacks camels, in the rump; (S, K;) so that when a she-camel rises, or is roused, her thighs tremble for a while, and then stretch out: (S:) or it is when there is a convulsive motion in the hind leg or the thighs of a camel, when he desires to stand up, or rises, or is roused, for a while, and then a stretching out of the same.

A certain vehicle for women, (S, * TA,) a thing smaller than the هَوْدَج: (S, K, TA:) pl. رَجَائِزُ: (TA:) or a [ garment of the kind called ] كِسَآء, (S, K, TA,) in which is a stone, (K, TA, [in the CK a while stone, ]) or in which are put stones, (S,) and which is suspended to one of the two sides of the هودج, to balance it, when it inclines: (S, TA:) so called because of its commotion: (TA:) or a thing consisting of a pillow and skins, or hides, put in one of its two sides for…
and رَجَّازَةٌ: see رَاجِزٌ; the latter, in two places.

One who utters, or recites, poetry, or verse, of the metre termed رَجَزٌ; who speaks in verse of that metre; who poetizes, or versifies, in that metre: and in like manner,, and [which signifies one who does so much ], and [one who does so very much ]. (TA.) El-'Ajjáj has been placed the highest in rank as a راجز. (Mz, 49th نوع.) [His son, Ru-beh, seems to occupy nearly an equal place.

A camel having the disease termed رَجَزٌ: fem. رَجْزَآءُ: (S, K:) the latter is explained as signifying weak in the rump, that does not move from her place unless after twice or thrice rising from the place where she lay: and that does not rise, when she desires to do so, unless after vehement trembling. (TA.) [Hence,] إِنَّهَا لَرَجْزَآءُ, said of the wind ( الرِّيح ), (assumed tropical:) Verily it is continuous, or lasting.
A poem of the metre termed رَجَزٌ: (Msb, K:) pl. أَرَاجِيزُ. (A, K.)
: see رَاجِزٌ; the former, in two places.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
